hero.headline: Trump-Linked Crypto Firm World Liberty Trust Granted Bank Status
hero.body:
World Liberty Trust, a cryptocurrency venture connected to former President Donald Trump, has received preliminary approval for bank status from federal regulators. The decision marks an unprecedented development for a sitting or former president's business venture to gain banking authority.

The Trump-appointed regulator overseeing the application approved the banking license for World Liberty Financial, the crypto company backing the trust. The approval allows the venture to operate with the legal powers of a chartered bank, including accepting deposits and making loans, though it will focus on cryptocurrency-related banking services.

Critics have raised questions about potential conflicts of interest, particularly given Trump's influence over the regulatory appointment process during his presidency. The approval process for banking charters typically involves extensive review of financial soundness, management competence, and compliance capabilities. The crypto industry has sought greater access to traditional banking infrastructure for years, facing resistance from regulators concerned about the volatility and risks associated with digital assets.

World Liberty Financial has positioned itself as a bridge between traditional banking and cryptocurrency markets. The preliminary approval represents a significant step toward full operational status, though the company must still meet additional regulatory requirements before beginning banking operations. The venture joins a small number of crypto-focused firms that have obtained banking charters in recent years.

The decision comes as the cryptocurrency industry continues to seek legitimacy within the traditional financial system. Banking status would allow World Liberty Trust to offer services that pure crypto companies cannot provide, potentially giving it a competitive advantage in the market. The approval process and the Trump family's involvement in the venture have drawn scrutiny from ethics watchdogs and political opponents who question whether the regulatory decision was influenced by political considerations.

cards.headline: U.S. and Iran approach deadline for peace and nuclear negotiations
cards.body:
The United States and Iran are moving past a deadline they set to reach an agreement on peace and Iran's nuclear program, with negotiations showing mixed signals about progress.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio told the Senate Foreign Relations Committee that Iran has agreed to discuss aspects of its nuclear program it had previously refused to negotiate. "There is the prospect before us, which could happen today, it could happen tomorrow, it could happen next week – that for the first time, certainly in my memory, they have agreed to negotiate aspects of their nuclear program that just a month ago" they would not, Rubio said.

However, Tehran announced it was halting peace talks and moving to fully close the Strait of Hormuz, citing Israeli military operations in Lebanon as a ceasefire violation. Iran's state-affiliated Tasnim News Agency reported that Tehran would stop exchanging messages with Washington through intermediaries. President Trump later disputed this, saying conversations "have been going on continuously."

Rubio outlined a two-phase framework for negotiations. Reopening the Strait of Hormuz is a precondition for talks, not a bargaining chip. This would require Iran to announce clearly it is not charging tolls, help remove mines it placed there, and commit not to fire on ships. Rubio rejected offering sanctions relief simply to reopen the vital waterway. "Any sanctions relief is condition-based," he said, and is tied to Iran's nuclear program.

Phase two would require Iran to commit to disposing of its stockpile of highly enriched uranium and to negotiate "severe and long-term limitations, and or cancellation of enrichment activity."

Regarding Iran's military capabilities, Rubio claimed the country's missile program had been "substantially degraded" and its drone-building capability "eroded." However, The New York Times reported in May that Iran had retained roughly 70 percent of its prewar missile stockpile. Analysts noted that over 85 percent of Iran's ballistic missile, drone and naval defense industrial base has been damaged or destroyed, though this may limit Iran's ability to replace weapons rather than indicating immediate military collapse.

The blockade the U.S. launched in April is costing Tehran "hundreds of millions of dollars a day" in lost oil revenue, according to Rubio. The ceasefire agreed in April had included an Iranian commitment to reopen the strait, but Trump later said Iran had "knowingly failed" to honor that pledge.

Rubio also claimed that Mojtaba Khamenei, who succeeded his father Ali Khamenei after the supreme leader was killed in February's opening strikes, was alive and increasingly engaged in the regime's efforts, though Khamenei has not been seen in public since assuming office.

cards.headline: Ukraine launches mass drone attack on Moscow region
cards.teaser: Ukraine targeted Moscow with hundreds of drones in one of the largest aerial assaults of the war.
cards.body:
Ukraine launched one of its largest aerial attacks of the war, deploying hundreds of drones across Russia. The assault killed at least six people, according to reports from the campaign.

The attack targeted Moscow and surrounding regions as Russia simultaneously conducted aerial bombardments across Ukrainian territory. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky accused Russia of targeting civilian infrastructure during its counterattacks.

cards.headline: Hurricane Lala batters Hawaii with high winds and heavy rain
cards.body:
Tropical Storm Lala is bringing hurricane-force conditions to Hawaii's Big Island with dangerous winds, heavy rainfall and high surf. The storm was located approximately 420 miles southeast of Hilo and was forecast to strengthen into a hurricane as it approached the islands.

The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration reported that Lala was packing winds of 60 mph as it moved toward the archipelago. Hurricane warnings have been issued for Hawaii county, which includes the Big Island, while tropical storm warnings cover Maui, Molokai and Kahoolawe.

Forecasters predict significant rainfall across the islands, with 8 to 12 inches expected on Maui and the Big Island. Some areas could see up to 25 inches. A storm surge of 1 to 3 feet is also forecast as the storm reaches shore. NOAA's Weather Prediction Center warned that Hawaii "faces life-threatening flash floods and mudslides as Tropical Storm Lala approaches."

Governor Josh Green declared a state of emergency, stating that Lala poses a serious threat to the state, particularly Hawaii Island. "Our state and county emergency teams are coordinating closely with federal partners," Green said. "I urge everyone to secure their homes, gather essential supplies, review their family emergency plans and follow updates from trusted official sources."

Hawaii county Mayor Kimo Alameda urged residents to prepare immediately for possible damaging winds, flooding rain, high surf, power outages, loss of communications and road closures. Residents have been advised to clear gutters and drains, move valuables off the ground, seal gaps in doors and remove tree limbs that could threaten their properties. Officials also warned people to stay away from beaches and coastal areas where rough surf and rip currents pose dangers.

If Lala's center passes over the Big Island, it will mark the first direct hit by a tropical cyclone there since Tropical Storm Darby in 2016. The last major hurricane to strike Hawaii was Hurricane Iniki in 1992, which caused at least six deaths and billions of dollars in damage.

The storm's approach coincides with a powerful El Niño forming in the central equatorial Pacific Ocean. The NOAA predicts a 69 percent chance of a historic El Niño event that would exceed the strength of previous events dating back to 1950 when it peaks between October and December. El Niño conditions typically promote hurricane activity in the Pacific while suppressing it in the Atlantic.

Hawaii Volcanoes National Park closed access to Mauna Loa's summit on Thursday afternoon, with plans to close the welcome center, trails and the Nahuku lava tube during the storm.

cards.headline: FDA Assigns Highest Risk Classification to Egg Recall Over Salmonella
cards.teaser: Nearly 1.6 million cartons of eggs received a Class I designation after dozens fell ill across multiple states.
cards.body:
The Food and Drug Administration elevated a massive egg recall to its highest-risk classification on August 12 following a salmonella outbreak. Nearly 1.6 million dozen white and brown cage-free eggs from Texas were recalled due to contamination concerns.

The outbreak has sickened nearly 100 people across multiple states. Health officials are continuing their investigation into the scope of illnesses linked to the contaminated eggs. The Class I designation reflects the serious health threat posed by the product.

cards.headline: Supreme Court faces emergency requests on Trump mail ballot restrictions and White House construction
cards.body:
The Supreme Court is considering emergency applications from the Trump administration during the justices' summer recess, including requests to revive mail ballot restrictions and allow construction to resume on a controversial White House ballroom project.

The White House ballroom dispute has become a significant test of presidential authority. The administration demolished the historic East Wing of the White House to make way for the planned $400 million ballroom, which Trump has described as "a gift" to the American people. A federal appeals court for the District of Columbia ruled last week that the project lacked necessary approval from Congress and ordered construction to halt.

The administration has asked the Supreme Court to keep the appeals court decision on hold while it prepares a full appeal. Solicitor General D John Sauer wrote in the filing that the case "involves an extraordinary and unlawful injunction that will halt the ongoing construction of the integrated military complex including a totally secure ballroom space, at the East Wing of the White House, which is vitally required by national security."

The government argues that every component of the project functions as "an integrated whole geared toward remedying security deficiencies and bringing critical improvements to the White House." According to the administration, the ballroom structure is designed to shield a military installation located beneath it.

The lower court ordered that aboveground work remain blocked until Congress approves the project, but allowed construction on underground security structures to continue. The appeals court paused its own ruling until August 21 to give the administration time to file its Supreme Court appeal. Chief Justice John Roberts set a Tuesday deadline for parties challenging the project to respond to the administration's request.

The National Trust for Historic Preservation, which sued to block the ballroom's construction, criticized the administration's legal strategy. The organization said the administration "brazenly asserted" that even if ballroom construction were unlawful, the Supreme Court would lack authority to stop it. The group called on the Supreme Court to reject what it described as "the administration's transparent efforts to evade the rule of law, frustrate judicial review, and limit the availability of meaningful relief in the courts."

The emergency docket activity places the Supreme Court back in a prominent position during its summer recess, which typically runs from late June through early October. During this period, the court does not hear oral arguments but continues to process emergency applications and administrative matters. Individual justices or the full court can act on such requests even while not in regular session.

The Trump administration has appealed multiple lower court decisions to the Supreme Court this week, following temporary injunctions related to the president's attempts to restrict mail-in voting.

cards.headline: Trump administration uses visa policy to assert dominance in Western Hemisphere
cards.teaser: The U.S. is trying to reassert control over the Americas through visa restrictions as part of an expansionist approach.
cards.body: As part of its strategy to reassert American influence in the Western Hemisphere, the Trump administration is leveraging U.S. visa policy as a diplomatic tool. Visa restrictions and approval processes are being used as leverage in relations with nations across the region, with control over visa access serving as a means of maintaining American influence over hemispheric affairs.

cards.headline: Russia launches aerial attacks across Ukraine, killing five
cards.teaser: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky accused Russia of targeting civilian infrastructure in fresh strikes.
cards.body:
Russia conducted aerial strikes across Ukraine, resulting in five deaths. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that Russia deliberately targeted civilian infrastructure. Moscow claimed that its operations hit a warehouse.

The attacks are part of the broader conflict between the two nations, which has involved repeated exchanges of aerial assaults. Ukraine has responded with significant drone strikes of its own, including one of the war's largest aerial campaigns that killed at least six people in Russia.

cards.headline: Ukraine launches mass drone attack on Moscow region
cards.teaser: Ukraine targeted Moscow with hundreds of drones in one of the largest aerial assaults of the war.
cards.body:
Ukraine launched one of its largest aerial attacks of the war, deploying hundreds of drones across Russia. The assault killed at least six people, according to reports from the campaign.

The attack targeted Moscow and surrounding regions as Russia simultaneously conducted aerial bombardments across Ukrainian territory. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky accused Russia of targeting civilian infrastructure during its counterattacks.

cards.headline: Qatar denies holding Iranian pilots after downing fighter jets
cards.teaser: Iran claims three pilots have been detained since Qatar shot down two fighter jets at the start of the U.S.-Iran war.
cards.body:
Qatar denied Iranian allegations that it is holding three Iranian pilots following the downing of two Iranian fighter jets. Iran claims the pilots have been detained since the jets were shot down at the beginning of the U.S.-Iran war.

Qatari officials rejected the accusations, disputing Iran's assertion that the pilots are being held. The incident occurred during the early stages of the conflict between the United States and Iran.

cards.headline: Indonesia earthquake kills at least 51, displaces thousands
cards.teaser: Hundreds of homes and public buildings sustained severe damage as rescue efforts continue.
cards.body:
A powerful 7.7-magnitude earthquake struck eastern Indonesia early Saturday, killing at least 47 people and causing widespread destruction across the Flores region. The quake collapsed numerous buildings and homes, prompting thousands of residents to flee to higher ground fearing a tsunami.

Rescue operations faced significant challenges as landslides blocked roads and disrupted communications to Nagekeo, the area nearest the epicenter. Rescuers struggled to reach affected communities to assess the full scale of casualties and damage across the seismic-prone region.

cards.headline: Cholera outbreak sickens over 90 in Myanmar's largest city
cards.teaser: Civil war and military rule have weakened the health care system while monsoon rains increase disease risk.
cards.body:
A cholera outbreak in Myanmar's biggest city has sickened more than 90 people. The spread of the waterborne disease comes as civil war and military rule have severely weakened the country's health care infrastructure.

Heavy monsoon rains have increased the risk of cholera and other waterborne illnesses across the region. The combination of conflict, governance challenges, and seasonal weather has created conditions conducive to the outbreak.

cards.headline: Ukrainian bank worker faces life in Russian prison on terrorism charges
cards.teaser: Artem Murdid, his mother, and his girlfriend are accused of terrorism, but they say they did nothing wrong.
cards.body:
A Ukrainian bank worker is facing life imprisonment in Russia after being charged with terrorism. Artem Murdid, along with his mother and girlfriend, are accused of terrorist activities, allegations all three deny.

The family maintains they did nothing wrong and are being prosecuted unjustly. The case highlights the treatment of Ukrainian citizens detained in Russia during the ongoing conflict between the two countries.

cards.headline: Indonesia earthquake leaves 51 dead, thousands displaced
cards.teaser: Rescue operations continue after a deadly earthquake severely damaged hundreds of buildings across Indonesia.
cards.body:
A 7.7 magnitude earthquake struck off the coast of Indonesia early Saturday, killing at least 51 people and injuring more than 100. The quake collapsed buildings across multiple regencies on Flores island, with the heaviest toll in Manggarai and East Manggarai. Additional deaths were reported in Sikka, Ngada and Ende regencies.

Rescue crews dug through collapsed buildings and landslide debris on Sunday as they searched for survivors and bodies. Thousands of residents were displaced as the earthquake damaged hundreds of homes and public buildings, rendering many structures uninhabitable or at risk of collapse.

cards.headline: Doctors push for greater focus on postpartum psychosis
cards.teaser: Medical professionals and survivors call for increased research and awareness of a severe postpartum mental health condition.
cards.body:
The high-profile murder trial of Lindsay Clancy has spotlighted postpartum psychosis, a severe mental illness affecting new mothers. The case has prompted doctors and women who have experienced the condition to advocate for increased attention and research.

Survivors of postpartum psychosis are calling for greater medical and public awareness. They emphasize the need for better understanding of the difficult-to-predict condition, arguing that improved recognition could help identify and support affected mothers sooner.

cards.headline: Samish Nation works to save critically endangered sunflower sea stars
cards.teaser: University researchers partner with a Northwest tribe to restore a species that has seen billions of deaths in the Pacific.
cards.body:
Sunflower sea stars, distinctive creatures with 24 arms, face critically endangered status in the Pacific Ocean following the deaths of billions of individuals. University of Washington researchers have partnered with the Samish Indian Nation to restore the species and bring it back from the brink of extinction.

The collaboration represents a shared commitment between scientific and Indigenous communities to address this dramatic population decline and preserve an important part of Pacific Ocean ecosystems.

cards.headline: Families return home after Stourbridge fires
cards.teaser: Residents evacuated from fires are discovering damage to their properties for the first time.
cards.body:
Families who fled fires in Stourbridge began returning to their homes on Sunday. Many residents are only now seeing the full extent of damage to their properties after being evacuated.

The fires forced numerous families to leave their homes as emergency crews worked to contain the blazes. The return process allowed displaced residents to assess whether their homes remained habitable and what repairs might be needed.

cards.headline: Bangladesh defeats Australia in historic cricket upset
cards.teaser: Bangladesh secured one of Test cricket's greatest upsets with a nine-wicket victory over Australia.
cards.body:
Bangladesh completed one of Test cricket's greatest upsets by defeating Australia by nine wickets on the fourth day of the series opener in Darwin. The emphatic victory showcased Bangladesh's capability to compete at the highest level of international cricket.

The dominant performance across both batting and bowling demonstrated Bangladesh's strength throughout the match. This historic win represents a significant milestone for Bangladesh cricket, marking a major achievement on Australian soil.

cards.headline: Ukraine launches major drone attack on Russia, killing six
cards.teaser: Hundreds of drones struck targets across Russia in one of the largest aerial assaults of the war.
cards.body:
Ukraine launched hundreds of drones across Russia on Sunday in one of its largest aerial operations since the war began, killing at least six people. The attack struck multiple locations throughout Russian territory, marking a significant escalation in Kyiv's long-range drone warfare campaign.

The scale of the assault demonstrates Ukraine's growing capability to conduct sustained aerial strikes deep into Russian territory, representing a notable shift in the conflict's dynamics.

cards.headline: Policymakers Push Tech Companies to Share AI Data Center Profits
cards.teaser: Officials across the country are working to ensure communities benefit financially from the expansion of artificial intelligence infrastructure.
cards.body:
Policymakers across the country are working to ensure tech giants share the profits generated by AI data centers. As these facilities expand, they impose significant costs on local communities through increased electricity demands and infrastructure strain.

Officials are developing various approaches to capture economic benefits for their regions, including tax agreements, revenue sharing arrangements, and requirements that companies invest in local infrastructure. The effort reflects recognition that while tech companies reap substantial profits from AI development, the communities hosting these data centers bear the operational costs.

cards.headline: Waymo Receives Approval to Expand Robotaxi Service Across California
cards.teaser: The autonomous vehicle company gained regulatory clearance to scale up operations and enter Sacramento and additional markets.
cards.body:
California regulators granted Waymo permission to significantly expand its robotaxi service throughout the state. The approval allows the company to increase operations in Los Angeles and Bay Area regions while entering new markets including Sacramento.

The expansion represents a major milestone for autonomous vehicle deployment in the nation's most populous state. Waymo's service map in the Bay Area could extend to areas like Bodega Bay. The regulatory green light positions the company to compete more broadly in California's transportation market.

cards.headline: Los Angeles Lakers Sold for Record $12.5 Billion
cards.teaser: The basketball franchise's sale price set a new high for sports team valuations, surpassing the $10 billion paid just last year.
cards.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers changed hands in a transaction valuing the team at $12.5 billion, establishing a new record for professional sports franchise sales. The price represents a 25 percent increase from the $10 billion the team commanded when it last sold in 2025.

The escalating valuations of major sports franchises reflect growing revenue from broadcasting rights, sponsorships, and international market expansion. The Lakers deal continues a trend of record-breaking sales prices across professional sports leagues, driven by wealthy investors viewing teams as prestigious assets with reliable income streams.

cards.headline: Harvard Invests $2.2 Billion in SpaceX
cards.teaser: The university's endowment made a substantial bet on Elon Musk's rocket and satellite company.
cards.body:
Harvard University disclosed a $2.2 billion investment in SpaceX, representing one of the largest institutional stakes in the private aerospace company. The investment from Harvard's endowment fund signals confidence in the commercial space industry's growth prospects.

SpaceX has expanded its business beyond rocket launches to include its Starlink satellite internet service and plans for interplanetary missions. The substantial investment from a major institutional investor like Harvard could influence other endowments and pension funds to increase their exposure to the private space sector.

cards.headline: Delayed Food Safety Rule May Have Slowed Cyclospora Outbreak Response
cards.teaser: A regulation that could have helped trace contamination sources faster was postponed by the Trump administration last year.
cards.body:
Food safety experts say a delayed rule could have helped investigators trace the cyclospora outbreak more quickly. The regulation was postponed by the Trump administration and would have strengthened tracing systems for produce moving through the food supply chain.

Cyclospora spreads through human waste and has proven difficult to track through the complex network of farms, distributors, and retailers supplying fresh produce to consumers. Critics argue that weakened food safety oversight has hampered efforts to identify contamination sources during this outbreak that has sickened thousands.

hero.headline: Google releases Pixel 11 series with focus on Gemini AI integration
hero.body:
Google Faces Major Copyright Lawsuit Over Gemini AI Training

Major publishers have filed a lawsuit against Google, claiming the company illegally used millions of copyrighted books to train its Gemini artificial intelligence system. The case, filed in federal court in New York, represents what the publishers describe as "one of the most prolific infringements of copyrighted materials in history."

The lawsuit was brought by Hachette Book Group, Cengage Learning, Elsevier, and bestselling author Scott Turow. The publishers argue that Google misused books originally provided for limited purposes through services like Google Books, Google Play Books, and Google Scholar. These platforms allowed Google to display searchable excerpts and sell ebooks, but the lawsuit claims Google went beyond these agreements by copying the works to train a commercial AI product.

According to the complaint, Google copied copyrighted books without permission or payment to build Gemini, despite internal discussions acknowledging potential legal risks. The filing states Google identified that it could face "10 billion to 100 billion dollars in potential fines" for using texts provided through Google Play Books. The publishers contend that Google's actions harm authors and the publishing industry, particularly as AI-generated content could replace sales of original works.

The suit includes a striking example of the concern. Gemini could generate "a 100-page murder mystery set in a quiet seaside town filled with secrets" in 20 minutes for 39 cents, potentially substituting for original copyrighted works on which the model trained. The publishers argue that "no publisher or author can compete with that."

The complaint names specific copyrighted books allegedly used without permission, including N.K. Jemisin's The Fifth Season and Lemony Snicket's Who Could That Be at This Hour?

This lawsuit adds to expanding legal battles over generative AI and copyright protections. Authors and publishers have filed multiple cases against Google, OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta, alleging unauthorized use of copyrighted works for AI training. A judge previously ruled in Meta's favor in a copyright case brought by authors. However, Anthropic recently agreed to pay 1.5 billion dollars to authors who alleged their pirated books trained the AI chatbot Claude.

Earlier this year, thousands of authors including Kazuo Ishiguro, Philippa Gregory, and Richard Osman published an "empty" book protesting AI firms' use of their work without permission.

This new case follows an earlier attempt by Hachette and Cengage to join an existing copyright lawsuit against Google filed by authors and illustrators in 2023. Google opposed their participation, prompting the publishers to launch separate legal action.

The plaintiffs are seeking statutory damages, an injunction preventing continued alleged infringement, and a court order requiring Google to destroy unauthorized copies used in training its AI systems. Google did not respond to requests for comment.

cards.headline: SpaceX sets record with two Falcon 9 launches 38 minutes apart
cards.teaser: The company launched rockets from separate facilities in rapid succession, carrying satellites for different missions.
cards.body:
SpaceX launched two Falcon 9 rockets just 38 minutes apart, setting a new record for the shortest time between launches by the company. One mission carried Globalstar satellites from Florida's Space Coast, while the other deployed 24 Starlink satellites from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California.

The back-to-back launches also included a mission for the U.S. Space Force. The rapid turnaround demonstrates SpaceX's operational capacity to conduct multiple launches from geographically separated facilities within the same hour, a capability that required coordination across launch sites and mission control teams.

cards.headline: Scientists propose new theory on the origin of the universe
cards.teaser: Researchers have developed a theory that could change fundamental physics concepts taught in textbooks.
cards.body:
A new theoretical framework about the universe's origin has been proposed by scientists, with implications significant enough to potentially require revisions to physics textbooks. The theory addresses fundamental questions about how the universe began.

The research represents a departure from current cosmological models. While the theory has been published, it will require further scientific review and testing before gaining widespread acceptance in the physics community.

cards.headline: Saturn moon Enceladus shows conditions potentially suitable for life
cards.teaser: The moon possesses water, chemistry, hydrothermal energy, and a long-lasting ocean, according to researchers.
cards.body:
Enceladus possesses nearly all the ingredients required to support life. The Saturnian moon contains water, suitable chemistry, hydrothermal energy sources, and an ocean capable of persisting across geological timescales.

Scientists view Enceladus as one of the solar system's most promising candidates in the search for extraterrestrial life. A comprehensive investigation that ultimately finds no life would itself represent a significant discovery for astrobiology, helping scientists understand the prevalence of life beyond Earth.

cards.headline: Research suggests birds may see Earth's magnetic field through quantum process
cards.teaser: Scientists believe migratory birds perceive magnetic fields superimposed on their vision through proteins in their eyes.
cards.body:
Migrating birds may visually perceive Earth's magnetic field overlaid on their surroundings, according to scientists studying avian navigation. Researchers believe this ability stems from a quantum reaction inside light-sensitive proteins called cryptochromes found in birds' eyes.

This mechanism would enable birds to see magnetic field lines as they travel, integrating directional information with their regular vision. The discovery offers insight into how birds successfully navigate across long-distance migrations.

cards.headline: Woman alleges stepfather used Grok AI to create explicit imagery from childhood photo
cards.teaser: The case highlights concerns about AI tools being used to generate inappropriate content from ordinary images.
cards.body:
A woman has accused her stepfather of using Grok AI to transform a childhood photograph into explicit imagery. She expressed concern that AI image generation tools are being misused to create child sexual abuse material from ordinary photos.

The case highlights significant gaps in safeguards protecting AI image generation systems from abuse. It underscores growing concerns about how artificial intelligence tools can be weaponized to produce illegal content from benign source material.

cards.headline: Disney reveals VisionQuest trailer at D23 fan event
cards.teaser: The entertainment company showcased upcoming projects including Marvel and Star Wars content.
cards.body:
Disney's D23 fan event opened with the debut of a VisionQuest trailer, continuing the Marvel Cinematic Universe's slate of upcoming projects. The event also showcased a teaser for Star Wars: Ahsoka season two, which launches January 20, 2027, featuring a darker, witchcraft-themed direction for the franchise.

The presentations included additional reveals for the Doomsday trailer and announcements regarding the MCU's X-Men integration and the Star Wars: Starfighter project. D23 remains Disney's flagship venue for unveiling new entertainment across its film and streaming platforms.

hero.headline: Makhachev breaks UFC record with 17th consecutive win
hero.body:
Islam Makhachev secured his 17th straight victory at UFC 330, establishing a new promotion record with a dominant performance against Ian Machado Garry. The lightweight champion's win solidifies his position as the best pound-for-pound fighter in the world.

Makhachev's unbeaten streak now stands as the longest consecutive winning run in UFC history. His victory over Machado Garry, a rising contender in the lightweight division, demonstrates his continued ability to overcome quality opposition while maintaining technical excellence throughout his career.

The fight served as the main event at UFC 330, held in Atlanta. The victory adds another significant achievement to Makhachev's legacy as he continues defending his championship while extending an unprecedented winning streak that separates him from other fighters in the promotion's history.

The achievement marks a major milestone in mixed martial arts. Makhachev's consistency and fighting style have established him as one of the most dominant forces the sport has seen. His record-breaking performance raises questions about potential future challengers and whether any current contender possesses the skills necessary to halt his momentum in the lightweight division.

With 17 consecutive victories now to his name, Makhachev has positioned himself at the pinnacle of modern MMA. His success reflects not only his technical abilities but also his capacity to adapt to different fighting styles and overcome varying types of opponents at the highest level of competition.

The lightweight champion's run shows no signs of slowing down. Each victory builds upon his growing reputation as one of the sport's greatest fighters. His record-setting performance at UFC 330 adds to an already impressive resume that includes multiple title defenses and consistently dominant performances against top-ranked competitors.

Makhachev's achievement comes as part of a broader landscape of record-breaking performances across combat sports and athletics. His milestone represents years of dedication, discipline, and high-level competition that have culminated in this historic winning streak.

As Makhachev looks ahead, potential challengers from the lightweight division will need to find ways to counter his technical superiority and fighting approach. His current form and winning streak suggest that maintaining his championship status and continuing this historic run remains well within his capabilities.

The victory at UFC 330 cements Makhachev's status not just as the current champion, but as one of the greatest lightweight fighters to ever compete in the UFC. His 17-fight winning streak stands as a testament to his elite-level abilities and his status among the sport's most dominant athletes.

cards.headline: Bangladesh defeats Australia in historic Test cricket upset
cards.teaser: Bangladesh secured a nine-wicket victory over Australia in Darwin, completing one of the biggest upsets in Test cricket history.
cards.body:
Bangladesh completed one of Test cricket's greatest upsets by defeating Australia by nine wickets on the fourth day of their series-opener in Darwin. The comprehensive victory over one of the sport's traditional powerhouses marked a historic achievement for the visiting team.

The result underscores Bangladesh's growing strength in Test cricket and represents a significant milestone for the nation's cricket program.

cards.headline: Pallister ends Ledecky's 14-year unbeaten streak in 800m freestyle
cards.teaser: Australian swimmer Lani Pallister handed Katie Ledecky her first international loss in the 800-meter freestyle, ending a streak that lasted more than a decade.
cards.body:
Australia's Lani Pallister defeated Katie Ledecky at the Pan Pacific Championships in Irvine, California, marking the American's first loss in the 800-meter freestyle at a major international meet. Pallister won with a championship record time of 8:06.10, while Ledecky finished second in 8:07.26. Leading from start to finish, Pallister's victory ended Ledecky's streak of 13 consecutive international 800m gold medals.

The result signals a shift in distance freestyle swimming, with Pallister emerging as a formidable competitor in an event long dominated by the American star. Ledecky's late-race charge, which has secured countless victories throughout her career, proved insufficient against Pallister's commanding performance.

cards.headline: Shields reclaims middleweight titles with sixth-round stoppage
cards.teaser: Claressa Shields stopped Kaye Scott in the sixth round to win the WBA and WBC middleweight championships in her return to the division.
cards.body:
Claressa Shields returned to middleweight in dominant fashion, stopping Kaye Scott in the sixth round to reclaim the WBA and WBC titles at State Farm Arena in Atlanta. Shields dropped Scott in the sixth before unleashing a sustained barrage that left Scott unable to continue, with her corner throwing in the towel at 1:38 of the round.

The five-division world champion and double Olympic gold medalist completed a remarkable 38-pound cut from heavyweight to middleweight for the fight. Shields has identified Lauren Price as her preferred next opponent following the impressive victory.

cards.headline: Djokovic loses at Cincinnati Open in first match since Wimbledon
cards.teaser: Novak Djokovic was eliminated from the Cincinnati Open in the second round by Thiago Agustin Tirante in his first tournament appearance since Wimbledon.
cards.body:
Novak Djokovic's return to competition ended in disappointment at the Cincinnati Open, where he fell to Argentina's Thiago Agustín Tirante 2-6, 6-4, 6-4 in the opening round. Despite winning the first set, Djokovic visibly struggled with the intense Ohio humidity, spending much of the match between points bent over and gasping for breath.

The defeat marked a significant breakthrough for Tirante, delivering the biggest win of his career against the former world number one. Djokovic's early exit from the tournament came in his first competitive match since Wimbledon.

cards.headline: Donnelly wins bronze as Britain takes team gold in European marathon
cards.teaser: Abbie Donnelly earned an individual bronze medal while Great Britain claimed team gold in the women's marathon at the European Championships.
cards.body:
Abbie Donnelly claimed bronze in the women's marathon at the 2026 European Championships in Birmingham. The British athlete's individual medal was complemented by a gold medal for Great Britain in the team event, marking a successful conclusion to the host nation's campaign at the championships.

The marathon competitions on the final day of the championships showcased strong performances from British distance runners, with the team gold adding to the nation's medal haul at the Birmingham event.

cards.headline: Dern retains 115-pound title with win over Robertson at UFC 330
cards.teaser: Mackenzie Dern successfully defended her 115-pound championship with a dominant victory over Gillian Robertson on the UFC 330 card.
cards.body:
Mackenzie Dern successfully defended her UFC strawweight title against Gillian Robertson at UFC 330, putting on a dominant performance that answered Robertson's pre-fight claims about grappling superiority.

The event featured Islam Makhachev's record-breaking main event victory over Ian Machado Garry. Makhachev extended his winning streak to 17 consecutive fights, cementing his status as the best pound-for-pound fighter in the world with a commanding performance.

hero.headline: Disney Announces Maleficent Roller Coaster and Villains Land Details for Magic Kingdom
hero.body:
Disney revealed new details about its upcoming Villains Land at Magic Kingdom during the D23 expo, including concept art and models for a Maleficent-themed roller coaster. The announcement marks one of the first villain-focused lands at a Disney park.

The new land will feature dark magic and ancient ruins as central design themes. Disney Parks Blog described the area as "delightfully bewitching" in its official announcement. The Maleficent roller coaster represents one of two new attractions planned for the expansion, with both rides serving as anchor attractions for the themed area.

The Villains Land will be located at Magic Kingdom in Walt Disney World's Florida resort. The project creates a dedicated space for Disney villain characters who traditionally serve as antagonists in the company's animated films. Maleficent, the villain from Sleeping Beauty, will serve as the centerpiece for one of the land's major attractions.

Disney executives presented concept models and artwork during the D23 expo showcasing the visual direction for the attractions. The roller coaster will incorporate theming based on Maleficent's character and design elements connected to her story. Specific operational details such as height, speed, or special effects were not disclosed during the initial announcement. The second ride planned for Villains Land was also revealed during the presentation, though limited details were shared about that attraction.

The Villains Land project represents a significant shift in Disney's approach to theme park design. Traditionally, Disney has emphasized heroes and princesses in its attractions, so this expansion focuses on the darker elements of Disney storytelling. The move reflects potential guest interest in villain-centered narratives and experiences.

This announcement comes alongside several other major Disney World expansion projects revealed at D23. The company announced that Monstropolis, a Monsters, Inc. themed land, will open at Disney's Hollywood Studios in 2027. Additionally, a new Indiana Jones attraction called "Indiana Jones and the Myth of the Jade Serpent" is in development for Disney's Animal Kingdom, featuring Harrison Ford reprising his iconic role as an animatronic character.

Michael Hundgen, Vice President Creative at Walt Disney World Portfolio for Walt Disney Imagineering, expressed enthusiasm about the company's expansion plans. These projects demonstrate Disney's ongoing commitment to developing new themed areas and attractions that appeal to diverse guest interests.

The Villains Land project represents a notable departure from Disney's historical emphasis on heroic characters, offering park visitors a chance to explore the stories and worlds of Disney's most memorable antagonists. The combination of the Maleficent roller coaster and a second unnamed attraction promises to create an immersive experience centered on darker Disney narratives.

cards.headline: Disneyland Plans Complete Reimagining of Tomorrowland Area
cards.teaser: Disney announced a full overhaul of Tomorrowland at Disneyland Park during the D23 expo.
cards.body:
Disney Parks executives announced plans to completely reimagine Tomorrowland at Disneyland Park during the D23 expo. The project will draw from Walt Disney's original vision for the futuristic-themed area of the park.

The announcement followed years of fan requests for updates to Tomorrowland. Disney's Experiences division chief discussed the refresh plans alongside other major park announcements at the expo. The reimagining represents one of the most significant overhauls planned for the California park.

cards.headline: Monsters Inc. Themed Land Monstropolis Set to Open at Disney World in 2027
cards.teaser: A Monsters Inc. themed area called Monstropolis will open at Disney's Hollywood Studios next year.
cards.body:
Monstropolis, a new land based on the Monsters Inc. film franchise, will open at Disney's Hollywood Studios in 2027. Disney announced the opening timeline during the D23 expo on Saturday. The themed area is currently under construction at the Florida park.

Michael Hundgen, Vice President Creative for Walt Disney World Portfolio at Walt Disney Imagineering, said the team was excited to bring Monstropolis to life for fans. The land will recreate the monster city from the Pixar animated films at Disney World.

cards.headline: Harrison Ford to Reprise Indiana Jones Role for New Disney Animal Kingdom Attraction
cards.teaser: Harrison Ford will return as Indiana Jones in a new Disney World ride opening at Animal Kingdom.
cards.body:
Harrison Ford will reprise his role as Indiana Jones for a new attraction at Disney's Animal Kingdom. The ride, titled Indiana Jones and the Myth of the Jade Serpent, was announced at D23 with details about Ford's involvement as an animatronic character and backstory elements.

Disney revealed the name and concept for the Indiana Jones attraction, which joins other adventure-themed experiences at the park. Ford's participation marks his return to the character for a Disney project following the film franchise.

cards.headline: Jury Seated for Trial in 1996 Tupac Shakur Murder Case
cards.teaser: A jury has been seated for the trial of Duane Keith Davis, charged in the 1996 killing of rapper Tupac Shakur.
cards.body:
Nearly 30 years after rapper Tupac Shakur was killed, a jury has been seated for the trial of Duane Keith Davis, known as Keffe D. Davis faces charges related to the fatal shooting that occurred in 1996. Former Death Row Records security personnel have called Davis a liar ahead of the trial proceedings.

Suge Knight, former Death Row Records executive, stated he does not want to testify in the trial. The case has drawn renewed attention as one of the most prominent unsolved murders in music history moves toward a courtroom resolution.

cards.headline: Robert Downey Jr. to Revive Iron Man Role for New Disney Avengers Project
cards.teaser: Robert Downey Jr. will return as Iron Man in a new Disney project following the Avengers films.
cards.body:
Robert Downey Jr. will reprise his role as Iron Man for a new Disney project. The announcement came during D23 presentations about Avengers Campus expansions and attractions. Downey's return marks a continuation of his portrayal of the character following the conclusion of the Avengers film series.

Disney also announced Avengers Infinity Defense, a new attraction set to open at Disneyland in 2028. The ride will feature Ms. Marvel in a lead role and include appearances from Avengers cast members.

cards.headline: Bruce Willis Attends Daughter Tallulah's Wedding in Rare Public Appearance
cards.teaser: Bruce Willis made a rare public appearance at his daughter Tallulah's wedding to Justin Acee.
cards.body:
Bruce Willis attended his daughter Tallulah Willis's wedding to Justin Acee at the family home in Idaho. The appearance marked a rare public outing for Willis amid his dementia care. Tallulah Willis shared details about a touching moment from the ceremony she said she would never forget.

The woodland-themed wedding took place at the Willis family property. Tallulah Willis is the daughter of Bruce Willis and Demi Moore. Vogue covered details of the ceremony and setting.

hero.headline: Supreme Court faces emergency requests on Trump mail ballot restrictions and White House construction
hero.body:
The Supreme Court is considering emergency applications from the Trump administration during the justices' summer recess, including requests to revive mail ballot restrictions and allow construction to resume on a controversial White House ballroom project.

The White House ballroom dispute has become a significant test of presidential authority. The administration demolished the historic East Wing of the White House to make way for the planned $400 million ballroom, which Trump has described as "a gift" to the American people. A federal appeals court for the District of Columbia ruled last week that the project lacked necessary approval from Congress and ordered construction to halt.

The administration has asked the Supreme Court to keep the appeals court decision on hold while it prepares a full appeal. Solicitor General D John Sauer wrote in the filing that the case "involves an extraordinary and unlawful injunction that will halt the ongoing construction of the integrated military complex including a totally secure ballroom space, at the East Wing of the White House, which is vitally required by national security."

The government argues that every component of the project functions as "an integrated whole geared toward remedying security deficiencies and bringing critical improvements to the White House." According to the administration, the ballroom structure is designed to shield a military installation located beneath it.

The lower court ordered that aboveground work remain blocked until Congress approves the project, but allowed construction on underground security structures to continue. The appeals court paused its own ruling until August 21 to give the administration time to file its Supreme Court appeal. Chief Justice John Roberts set a Tuesday deadline for parties challenging the project to respond to the administration's request.

The National Trust for Historic Preservation, which sued to block the ballroom's construction, criticized the administration's legal strategy. The organization said the administration "brazenly asserted" that even if ballroom construction were unlawful, the Supreme Court would lack authority to stop it. The group called on the Supreme Court to reject what it described as "the administration's transparent efforts to evade the rule of law, frustrate judicial review, and limit the availability of meaningful relief in the courts."

The emergency docket activity places the Supreme Court back in a prominent position during its summer recess, which typically runs from late June through early October. During this period, the court does not hear oral arguments but continues to process emergency applications and administrative matters. Individual justices or the full court can act on such requests even while not in regular session.

The Trump administration has appealed multiple lower court decisions to the Supreme Court this week, following temporary injunctions related to the president's attempts to restrict mail-in voting.

cards.headline: House Democrats question Navy on conditions aboard USS Abraham Lincoln after extended Middle East deployment
cards.teaser: A group of House Democrats sent a letter to the Acting Secretary of the Navy probing conditions on the USS Abraham Lincoln after the ship spent over 260 days docked in the Middle East.
cards.body:
House Democrats, including Representatives Joe Courtney and Maggie Goodlander, have sent a letter to Acting Secretary of the Navy Hung Cao expressing concerns about the USS Abraham Lincoln. The aircraft carrier has remained deployed to the Middle East for more than 260 days since November.

Sailors aboard the ship have faced significant hardships, including food shortages and broken plumbing. Some crew members have reportedly considered extreme measures to leave the vessel. A replacement carrier has been dispatched to relieve the Lincoln as scrutiny over the extended deployment continues.

cards.headline: Navy considers redesigning aircraft carriers to match Trump aesthetic preferences
cards.teaser: The United States Navy is potentially redesigning incoming aircraft vessels to align with President Trump's preferred aesthetic for the ships.
cards.body:
Original Card Text

The Navy is considering changes to Ford-class ships to match President Trump's preference for new aircraft carriers to resemble World War II-era vessels, according to a report from the Washington Post. The maritime branch is evaluating the potential redesign as part of requests from the president.

The proposed aesthetic changes would affect incoming aircraft carriers currently in development. The Ford-class carriers represent the Navy's newest generation of aircraft carriers, replacing the older Nimitz-class ships.

---

cards.headline: Democrats propose multiple Supreme Court overhaul plans as midterms approach
cards.teaser: As the midterm elections near, Democrats are advancing proposals to reshape the Supreme Court, including adding justices and limiting their terms.
cards.body:
As the midterms approach, Democrats are pushing several proposals to reshape the Supreme Court. Their plans include expanding the number of justices and imposing term limits on judicial appointments.

The reform efforts reflect Democratic frustration with recent Supreme Court decisions. The various proposals represent different approaches to changing how the high court operates.

cards.headline: Ocasio-Cortez leads 2028 Democratic presidential betting markets
cards.teaser: Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez now leads the field for the 2028 Democratic presidential nomination on major betting platforms Kalshi and Polymarket.
cards.body:
Speculation about a potential presidential run by Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez in 2028 has reached new heights, with the New York Democrat now topping betting markets for the Democratic nomination. She leads on both Kalshi and Polymarket, the two best-known political betting platforms.

The development signals growing attention to Ocasio-Cortez as a potential presidential candidate, though she has not announced any plans to run. The betting market rankings reflect wagering activity rather than polling or formal campaign infrastructure.

cards.headline: Democratic Socialists face key Florida primary after Wisconsin loss
cards.teaser: The Democratic Socialists of America face their last major midterm primary test in Florida after a loss in Wisconsin dealt a blow to the movement.
cards.body:
The Democratic Socialists of America are mounting their final major midterm primary push on Tuesday in Florida's 25th Congressional District. The contest comes after the organization suffered a setback in Wisconsin earlier this week, dealing a blow to the far-left movement's efforts to elect candidates aligned with its platform.

The Florida primary represents a critical moment for DSA as it works to expand its influence during the midterm election cycle. The race will demonstrate whether the organization can rebound from its recent loss and maintain momentum heading into November's general election battles.

cards.headline: Wisconsin Republican gubernatorial nominee Tom Tiffany declines to say if Trump will campaign with him
cards.teaser: Representative Tom Tiffany avoided questions about whether President Trump will join him on the campaign trail in his bid to become Wisconsin's governor.
cards.body:
Original Card Text (Unchanged)

The Republican nominee for Wisconsin governor sidestepped questions when asked if he expected President Trump to campaign with him. Appearing on Newsmax, Tiffany was asked by host Sharla McBride if Trump would join him on the trail as the president has done for other GOP candidates.

Trump has campaigned for various Republican candidates in races across the country. Tiffany is currently serving as a U.S. Representative from Wisconsin and is now seeking the governorship.
